name: Albanian
confidence_why: Trommer & Grimm 2004, Canalis 2008 and Coretta et al. 2023 agree that Albanian stress falls on the last syllable of the stem when it is closed or ends in a full non-mid vowel and otherwise on the penult, with inflection never moving it, and Newmark et al. 1982 and Matasović 2012 describe the same facts as regular stem-final stress with penultimate exceptions, so the placement is settled and the only disagreement is which case is called the default.

new_statements.quote: Early Proto-Albanian probably had a dynamic stress on the first syllable. Early Latin loan-words stressed on the penultimate lost the unstressed initial syllable(s), cf. L amīcus >> Alb. mik ‘friend’, L imperātor >> Alb. mbret ‘king’, L vicīnus >> Alb. fqinj ‘neighbour’. In contemporary language the stress is regularly on the last syllable of the stem, but there are exceptions, cf. lúle ‘flower’ (but muzé ‘museum’), jétë ‘life’ (but këtë’ ‘this’), etc. It is possible that Proto-Albanian still had free stress, because this assumption helps us understand some vowel changes in word-final position, e. g. the development of stressed final *-ā to -e, but unstressed *-ā to -ë (on which see below).

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog's StressTyp2 record encodes Albanian as fixed penultimate at word level (penultimate stress). Matasović instead makes the STEM the domain and puts the default on the LAST syllable of the stem, treating penultimate-stressed words (lúle, jétë) as exceptions — so the default placement differs (stem-final vs word-penult) and the type differs (morphologically bounded vs fixed positional). The two agree on the surface forms lúle and jétë; they disagree on muzé, këtë, and on consonant-final stems (mbret, fqinj, mik) where Matasović's rule gives final stress. Matasović is compatible with the catalog's Coretta et al. 2023 / Trommer & Grimm 2004 note (stress final, penult or antepenult at…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the modern language stress falls regularly on the last syllable of the stem (inflectional endings are not stressed), so a consonant-final or vowel-final stem is stressed on its final syllable (mbret, fqinj, mik, muzé, këtë); words like lúle 'flower' and jétë 'life' with penultimate stress are listed as exceptions. Historically: Early Proto-Albanian probably had initial dynamic stress; Proto-Albanian may have had free stress.
new_statements.exceptions: lúle 'flower' and jétë 'life' (penultimate) are given as exceptions to stem-final stress, contrasted with muzé 'museum' and këtë 'this' (final). No systematic account of the exceptions (no weight or vowel-quality condition) is given.
new_statements.identity_note: Matasović describes the modern standard (Tosk-based) literary language in 1908 Monastir orthography, which is the variety tosk1239 stands for; the stress section names no dialect. The sketch also mentions Old Gheg only for vowel length (sec. 3.2), not stress. The downloaded file is the author's 2024 revision of the 2012 sketch (same title, same URL family), 70 pp rather than 47.

readall_conflicts: Matasović (2012/2024, sec. 3.1, p. 8) states that stress is regularly on the last syllable of the stem with lexical exceptions (lúle, jétë penultimate), whereas the catalog's StressTyp2 record codes Albanian as fixed word-penultimate. The disagreement is over the default and the domain: StressTyp2 = penult of the word; Matasović = final syllable of the stem, penult-of-stem words being exceptions. 4-6) says stress is 'virtually always on the last or penultimate vowel of the stem', with consonant-final stems stressed finally and open-syllable stems penultimately, and Trommer & Grimm 2004 (cited in the catalog's Coretta 2023 note) give a stem-based weight/vowel-quality algorithm; on that view the StressTyp2 penult coding captures the open-syllable stems (lúle, jétë, púnë) and Matasović's stem-final default captures the consonant-final and i/a/u-final stems. Neither Matasović nor StressTyp2 mentions secondary stress.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Both deciding quotations are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated slides/page (T&G 2004 slides 3,5,7,8,9; Coretta et al. 2023 JIPA 53(3):1135). (2) The classification rests on 2004 conference slides plus a 2023 JIPA Illustration that gives only the three-syllable window and defers to Trommer & Grimm for predictability; the held Newmark et al. 1982 reference grammar independently states stem-final stress with stress-neutral inflection. Three open items downloaded now (Canalis 2008 IGG33 pp.1-14; Trommer GLOW abstract; Bermúdez-Otero 2007 handout) all agree on stem domain, right-edge, inflection-neutral, closed-final-syllable-attracts-stress; Canalis argues for pure quantity sensitivity (uneven trochee on the stem) and against the vowel-quality factor, which refines but does not overturn a 'weight-hedged, right edge, CVC heavy, non-strict' coding. sources.citation: Sawicka, Irena, Artur Karasiński & Andrzej Żak. 2026. Acoustic correlates of Albanian word stress in relation to the Balkan Slavic environment. Russian Linguistics 50(1): 19 (16 pp.). doi:10.1007/s11185-026-09346-w
sources.quote: We propose the following rule for Kosovo Albanian: the stressed vowel is the first lengthened vowel in the word. This represents a statistical (not absolute) tendency, with the stressed-unstressed duration ratio approximating 3:2 (in the paradigmatic test) or 5:3 (in syntagmatic analysis). Neither intensity nor F0 reliably marks stress, while vowel quality shows only minor, non-systematic variation. [...] it cannot be said that unstressed vowels undergo reduction in Albanian. | On placement: In verbs, stress is generally on the last syllable of the stem, while in nouns and adjectives (with numerous exceptions often related to stress-attracting suffixes) it falls on the penultimate syllable of the stem (Demiraj, 2002, p. 65; cf. also Bevington, 1974).

sources.quote: Во албанскиот јазик, акцентот е фиксиран, и во номиналната и во глаголската флексија, на пр. v│ajzë ‘девојка’, det. v│ajza, pl. det. v│ajzat, gen., dat. pl. v│ajzave итн. || Во албанскиот јазик, акцентот најчесто паѓа на последниот слог од зборообразувачката основа, но има многу исклучоци, кои најчесто се поврзани со тоа што многу наставки го привлекуваат акцентот, на пр. punët│or ‘работник’, sport│ist ‘спортист’ и др. Интерпретациите, засновани на современите теории, особено оптималната и метричката теорија, формулираат правила од фонетска природа. Така, според Каналис (Canalis 2007), нагласена е претпоследната мора на зборот.
sources.note: marginal: Examines the three-syllable accent-placement restriction and double accentuation in Balkan (mainly Macedonian) dialects, disputing a shared accentual system with Albanian dialects of the region.

sources.quote: 'In Albanian, uninflected words (e.g. nominative indefinite nouns) have final stress if the final syllable is closed (1a), or ends in a non-reduced non-mid vowel (1b,c), while stress falls on the penultimate syllable if the final syllable ends in a mid vowel (1d,e) (Bevington, 1974; Trommer, 2005). In forms with inflectional affixes ... stress is on the same syllable as in corresponding uninflected forms' (adét/adét-in, qershí/qersh-ín, hatá, hóle, bábo).
